title: Tanrei design system layer
description: A design system expressed as a layer over Tanrei's vocabulary. A layer changes values — dials, palettes, per-token rules — and adds tokens only through its `vocabulary`, additively and with a rationale. Every system descends from the root layer `core`: the default system `tanrei` and the presets extend it, and a product extends one of them.

extends.description: Id of the parent layer — an id, never a path. Only the root layer `core` omits it.

specVersion.description: Version of the role table. Bump when role rules change meaningfully.

components.description: Which components, and which values of a component's `variant` prop, this system ships. A layer starts from what its parent ships and changes it: `omit` leaves components out, `include` brings back ones an ancestor left out, `variants` does the same for the values of a component's `variant` prop. What an ancestor left out stays out unless a layer includes it again. The root layer leaves nothing out.

omit.description: component name (specs/inventory.json) → why this system leaves it out, and what it uses instead.

reason.description: Why this system does not ship the component.

insteadUse.description: The components this system ships for the same job, in order of preference.

include.description: Components an ancestor left out that this system ships again.

variants.description: component name → the values of its `variant` prop this system leaves out (`omit`) or brings back (`include`). The default value and at least one other stay.

attribution.description: For a layer that imitates another design system: what it is inspired by and under which license its values were obtained. Rendered into NOTICE and the docs.

palettes.description: Declared palettes. Later layers replace a palette of the same name; `null` drops an inherited one (its roles leave this system, so anything that pointed at them must be re-pointed).

description.description: Required when `roles` is set on a palette that is not a core intent: why does this system need it? It becomes the one-product rationale of the generated roles.

tones.description: Exact colors for single tones (0–100), e.g. a published ramp tuned by hand or a brand color that must not be recomputed. Every other tone is generated from the seed (or hue and chroma).

roles.description: Generate the four roles of an intent for this palette: <name>, on-<name>, <name>-container, on-<name>-container, with contrast checks.

tokens.description: Per-token operations, keyed by token id. The id must exist: in core, or declared under `vocabulary` by this layer or an ancestor.

rules.description: Pattern rules for per-state component tokens. `*` matches one id segment and is available as $1, $2… in the operation. An explicit entry in `tokens` beats a pattern; among patterns, fewer wildcards win, then the later layer.

vocabulary.description: Extensions of the vocabulary declared by this layer. `vocabulary` says that something exists; `tokens` and `rules` give it a value. Additive only: an id that core or an ancestor layer already declares cannot be declared again. Three kinds, told apart by shape: a token (`$type`) inside Tanrei's tree — a step in a series; an axis value (`from`) keyed `tanrei.comp.<component>.<axis>.<value>` — or, in a sys series whose steps are groups of tokens, a whole step cloned with `from` (a named spring set, `tanrei.sys.motion.spring.<scheme>.<name>`); a token in this layer's own namespace (`<layer id>.(sys|comp).…`).

$type.description: Optional assertion; it must match the vocabulary's type.

$value.description: An alias ("{tanrei.sys…}") re-points the token. A literal pins it, exempt from dials, and needs `reason`. For a choice of kind (tanrei.sys.behavior.*) the literal is one of the token's names ("ripple") or its index. For a fontFamily it is the font stack: named families first, then a system or generic fallback.

scale.description: Multiply the inherited definition by N without restating it. For typography, a map of fields.

operation.description: `$value` and `derive` may be combined on a typography token: `$value` pins the named fields (say lineHeight and fontWeight) and `derive` rules the rest (fontSize, letterSpacing).

declaredToken.description: A new token. It needs a value: inline here (`$value` + `reason`, an alias, or `derive`), or under `tokens`.

rationale.description: Why this design system or product needs the distinction. Shown wherever the token is shown.

$value.description: An alias ("{tanrei.sys…}") re-points the token. A literal pins it, exempt from dials, and needs `reason`.

onRole.description: For a color role: the role drawn on top of it. Registers the pair with the contrast invariants.

declaredAxisValue.description: A value cloned from an existing one. On a component axis (a size, a variant): every member token of the axis is cloned from the `from` value; `scale` multiplies the numeric members, still following the dials. In a sys series whose steps are groups of tokens (a named spring set, `tanrei.sys.motion.spring.<scheme>.<name>`): the whole group is cloned from the sibling `from`, so it can never be half a spring; `scale` does not apply. Override single members under `tokens`.

from.description: The existing value of the same axis — or the existing step of the same series — to start from.

scale.description: Multiply the inherited definition by N without restating it. For typography, a map of fields.

rule.description: One rule of the closed, declarative rule language: mul, scale, clamp, em (numeric — packages/token-engine/src/rules.js) and tone, alpha, mix, contrast-pick (color — palette.js for color roles, states.js for per-state component tokens). `{ "fixed": "<reason>" }` keeps a literal. On a typography token the rule is a map of field → rule (fontSize, letterSpacing). No addition, conditionals, strings or functions of your own.

tone.description: 0–100. A number; [standard, medium, high]; or { "light": […], "dark": […] }. Legal on a color role and on a per-state component color (an explicit tone per state: rest 80, hover 70, pressed 40).

on.description: The color token the result must be readable on.

from.description: The candidates. The one with the highest WCAG contrast against `on` wins, decided per scheme; the first wins a tie. On a color role: color roles or {tanrei.ref.palette.<palette>.<tone>}.
